html:
Panchala was an ancient kingdom of north India in the land between the Ganges and the Yamuna, one of the strongest states of the late Vedic period and later one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.

Panchala was a close ally of Kuru, its neighbour to the north west. Together they were the heartland where much of the later Vedic literature was composed. Panchala was split into a northern half, with its capital at Ahichchhatra, and a southern half around Kampilya. In the epic Mahabharata, Draupadi is the princess of Panchala.

By the 6th century BCE it had lost its lead to rising kingdoms further east, and it was later absorbed by Magadha. The region kept its weight: its old city of Kanyakubja grew into Kannauj, a capital of north India a thousand years later.
sum: Panchala was an ancient kingdom of north India in the land between the Ganges and the Yamuna, one of the strongest states of the late Vedic period and later one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas.
